definitions.note: plural, as in 'the picture of health': a perfect specimen

indicators.note: food that is cooked has been worked over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe note praising flawless pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' turns the letters of PIE-CRUST into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone looking the very image of health is called 'the picture of health', so ideal specimens fit.

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: to dominate someone is to possess or control them

explanation.surface: Police forces dominating the scene, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the last S from POSSESS. A posse is a band of men gathered by a sheriff.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a group summoned to help enforce the law, like a body of constables.

clue.text: Tale going about, after church, in Swiss Cottage

indicators.note: after says the church piece comes before the rest
going about suggests turning round, so the letters of tale are rearranged

explanation.surface: A story doing the rounds after a service, set in a Swiss holiday home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going about' scrambles the tale, and 'after' puts the church first. Swiss Cottage is also a London district, which disguises the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a wooden mountain house of the type built in Switzerland.

parts.note: a jockey in the saddle is said to be 'up'
a set is a group or class, as a school set

explanation.surface: Someone takes a tumble during a riding lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riding-class' looks like one thing, a lesson; split it after 'riding', since a jockey in the saddle is 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset something is to knock it over or unsettle it.

clue.text: Call to begin fencing English garden, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that these letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a fence round an English garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the garden, after the abbreviation for English. 'fencing' is the sport, not putting up a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: The French cry 'en garde' tells a swordsman to take guard before a bout.

indicators.note: battered means knocked about, so the letters of wives are rearranged

explanation.surface: Abused wives who were left reeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battered' rearranges the wives, and the abbreviation for left follows. 'spin' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To swivel is to turn or rotate on a pivot.

indicators.note: stormy suggests turbulence, so the letters of south-wind are thrown about

explanation.surface: Puzzling events brought on by a gale from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stormy' rearranges SOUTHWIND into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Detective novels built around solving a murder are called mysteries.

clue.text: Energy of six, initially taking on Italy trip

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter of the word taking
a trip is a stumble, so the letters of Italy fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Half a dozen people setting off on a lively Italian tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives T from 'taking'; 'trip' rearranges ITALY into ALITY. 'trip' looks like a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitality is liveliness, a store of physical vigour.

parts.note: reads like batches packed for the post, but the deliveries are births and the sets are tiny clothes for the newborn

explanation.surface: Little packs waiting at the depot to be dispatched.
explanation.definitionFit: A layette is the complete outfit of clothing and bedding prepared for a baby before its birth.

clue.text: Celebrity autograph of Leo for example

parts.note: a celebrity is a star
to autograph is to sign

explanation.surface: A famous person's signature, perhaps from someone called Leo.
explanation.walkthrough: Leo looks like a celebrity's first name; it is the zodiac lion.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo is one of the twelve divisions of the zodiac used in astrology.

indicators.note: inside says the abbreviation for right sits within the college

parts.note: POLY is short for polytechnic, a kind of college

explanation.surface: A company keeping its legal rights within a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts the right abbreviation into the college. 'Corporation' is old British slang for a large belly, not a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A portly person is stout, carrying a paunch.

indicators.note: without end means the last letter of the word is removed

parts.note: the world is the globe

explanation.surface: A ball-shaped lump, part of a never-ending world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without-end' drops the final E of GLOBE.
explanation.definitionFit: A glob is a lump or blob of something soft.

indicators.note: kind of hints at a sort or version, so these letters form a variant arrangement

explanation.surface: A register of voters listed alphabetically from A to E and onwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' rearranges ROLL, AE and ETC into the answer; the whole clue also describes an alphabetical register of voters.
explanation.definitionFit: The electoral roll is the official list of people entitled to vote, kept in alphabetical order.

clue.text: A place to rest in France, in the dark

parts.note: UN is the French for a
LIT is the French for a bed

explanation.surface: Somewhere a traveller in France can rest overnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in France' asks for French words: UN for 'A' and LIT for a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unlit has no light, leaving it dark.

definitions.meaning: a hollow in a hillside or rock
the Latin for 'beware', once shouted by British schoolboys as a lookout's alarm

explanation.surface: An empty threat from pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: British public-school slang used the Latin 'beware' as the cry that a master was coming.
explanation.definitionFit: A hollow underground chamber, and the old lookout's cry 'keep watch', both share this spelling.

clue.text: Interviews with monarch, perhaps, in houses

definitions.meaning: formal meetings granted by a sovereign or pope
a theatre's house is the crowd watching

explanation.surface: Royal interviews held in various residences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like buildings; in theatre the house is the spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal royal meetings and the spectators at a show both take this word.

clue.text: British fibre makes one see red

parts.note: istle is a coarse plant fibre from agave, used for cord

explanation.surface: Some British material causes anger.
explanation.walkthrough: ISTLE is a little-known Mexican fibre. 'makes one' joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To bristle is to react with sudden anger, like an animal raising its hackles.

parts.note: food that has gone off is of poor quality
a stage is a stagecoach

explanation.surface: A shabby bus hidden from spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is AUDIENCES: what happens out of sight of them is in the wings. 'coach' looks like a trainer.
explanation.definitionFit: Action happening in the wings, beyond the view of theatregoers, is out of their sight.

parts.note: reads as writing music, but composing here means calming someone down

explanation.surface: The work of writing music.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedation is the process of calming a person, often with drugs, which settles or composes them.

clue.text: Long-off, perhaps, if sent back to tree

indicators.note: sent back means the little word if is turned round

parts.note: an elder is a small tree

explanation.surface: A cricket shot hit far towards a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns the little word round before the tree. Long-off is a cricket fielding position near the boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: A player in a fielding position such as long-off is one of the side in the field.

definitions.meaning: a spread of spots on the skin

explanation.surface: A thoughtless eruption.
explanation.definitionFit: Reckless behaviour and a skin eruption share the word.

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A routine distress call: just phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a telephone call; it is the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something middling is ordinary, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Esparto growing wild in Barcelona, perhaps

indicators.note: growing wild suggests disorder, so the letters of esparto are scattered

explanation.surface: Esparto grass running wild in a Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing wild' rearranges ESPARTO, the Spanish grass, which fits the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Barcelona is a harbour city on the Mediterranean, an example of a port town.

indicators.note: out of here means the letters of breath are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A young woman who is panting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' rearranges BREATH.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertha is a woman's first name.

definitions.meaning: backing someone, as in being right there for them

explanation.surface: Propping up one's rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Backing a cause and a person's rump both take the word.

definitions.meaning: agitation, as in 'getting into a lather'

explanation.surface: Total alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective meaning total; it is the verb 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare something and a flustered condition ('in a right one') share the word.

parts.note: reads as a big lungful, but 'deep' is the ocean and the breath is a light wind

explanation.surface: Inhaling hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle wind blowing off the ocean is the ocean's exhalation.

clue.text: Having come up from Paris, engaged?

indicators.note: from tells you to take the letters out of the words Paris and engaged

explanation.surface: Someone arrived from Paris, now betrothed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' points to the letters running across the end of Paris and the start of engaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something risen has ascended, like the sun or dough.

parts.note: piece is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A gun for every person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' as slang for a handgun is mainly American.
explanation.definitionFit: Priced at a sum per item means each costs that.

clue.text: Painter brought back in Magritte's sorrowful period

indicators.note: brought back says the letters are read from right to left
in says the letters lie within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A Belgian surrealist's gloomy phase in art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points into 'Magritte's sorrowful', giving ITTESSOR, and 'brought back' turns it round. Magritte is a red herring painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante Gabriel Rossetti was a Pre-Raphaelite artist.

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters of Sterne take a new form

explanation.surface: Asking whether a book is by one writer or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book; it signals rearranging STERNE. Hemingway's first name gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The American writer Hemingway's forename is this.

definitions.meaning: a model or benchmark to follow

explanation.surface: A design used on a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal, a benchmark, and a banner are three senses of the same word.
